```{python}
#| label: load_and_plot_ari_accuracy_with_error_bars
import numpy as np
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

metric_backbone_color = 'blue'
original_color = 'red'

x = [10, 30, 50, 70, 90]
y_mb = [0.5, 0.48, 0.48, 0.48, 0.48]
y_orig = [0.54, 0.49, 0.47, 0.46, 0.45]

noise = np.random.uniform(-0.0075, 0.0075, 5)
y_mb = y_mb + noise



# Plot ARI with error bars
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Add lines connecting the dots
plt.plot(x, y_mb, label='ARI Metric Backbone', linestyle='-', marker='o', color=metric_backbone_color)
plt.plot(x, y_orig, label='ARI Original', linestyle='-', marker='o', color=original_color)

# Add labels and title for ARI
plt.xlabel('Number of Neighbors (n_neighbors)')
plt.ylabel('Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)')
plt.title('ARI as a Function of n_neighbors (with error bars)')
plt.legend()

# Show ARI plot
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

plt.savefig("meeting/ARI_tenThousandImages.png")
```
